findings_qualitative.value: CO outflow is monopolar to the north-east, a hollow cone, with an inner shell at z>2" and tentative on-axis knot

evidence.quote: we detect signatures of an inner knot close to the source (z $\simeq$ 0.25$^{\prime\prime}$) and of an inner shell at large distances (z $>$ 2$^{\prime\prime}$)

claims.hypothesis: Does the CO cavity trace a slow disk wind?
claims.experiment: Ring fits to transverse pv diagrams of disk-subtracted 12CO
claims.result: Conical flow 35 deg, constant Vp 9.3 km/s, rotation in disk sense, j=38 au km/s
claims.finding: Compatible with photoevaporative or MHD disk wind with launching radii 0.5-7 au

evidence.quote: The derived morphology and kinematics of the CO cavity are compatible with expectations from a slow disk wind

claims.hypothesis: Is the 18 au binary orbital scenario consistent with CO wiggling?
claims.experiment: Compare predicted orbital and precession wiggles with measured centroid velocities and positions
claims.result: Orbital solution predicts 1.5 km/s variations, not observed; precession solution matches
claims.finding: Orbital scenario ruled out (if disk wind); circumbinary-disk precession with close binary favoured

evidence.quote: our ALMA observations rule out the 18 au binary orbital scenario previously proposed to account for the wiggling of the optical jet

claims.hypothesis: Does the continuum disk have an inner hole?
claims.result: Constant flux within 3 sigma out to 75 au
claims.finding: No inner hole, contradicting Guilloteau et al. 2008

evidence.quote: We do not detect an inner hole in the continuum image, unlike the previous finding by (cite: guilloteau08).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Entrainment by wide-angle wind: constant Vr inconsistent with homologous expansion; stationary cavity from bow shocks remains possible

evidence.quote: is not consistent with the homologous expansion law $\overrightarrow{V} \propto \overrightarrow{Z}$ predicted by (cite: lishu96)

limitations_admitted.value: Launching-radius inferences rely on a steady-state assumption; ACA data would be needed to rule out an envelope

evidence.quote: Although ACA observations would be required to image this component fully and definitely rule out an envelope around HH30

referee_caveats_inferred: Disk-subtraction assumes perfect north-south disk symmetry in 12CO
Excitation temperature of 30 K is only a lower limit, so mass and mass flux are lower limits
Wiggle amplitude is near noise (~1 au offsets)
Binary constraints are conditional on a steady disk-wind origin
